pass_a_gloss: But also since the sowing one went out for the sowing, let us show that our soul received his seed neither as the ones by the road nor as the rocky places nor as the thorns, but as the good ground. That then neither by the road nor onto the thorns the word of Jesus came, to the extent that is upon us, in the Lord we will boast. For we have understood the things being said; on which account the wicked one did not seize the thing sown in our heart. And that it was not sown onto the thorns either, many will testify for us, observing that neither the anxiety of this age nor the cheating of the wealth nor the pleasures of the living have been able to block the word of God in our souls. Left over it is for the humans to be in two minds whether onto the rocky places or onto the fine ground the word of God came, to the extent that is upon us. For there has come about pressure and chasing because of the word, and there has set in a season of great testing, when the one sown onto the rocky places is being convicted, and those not going deep, nor receiving Jesus as far as the depth of the soul; but the one understanding the word bears fruit and holds down the word until the end in endurance, making a hundred times as much. For we hear in what manner the writing, setting beside us those who in a season of pressure or chasing are tripped up after the seeming in joy to have taken over the holy learnings, and tripped up by their not having root but believing toward a season, says according to Matthew: the one sown onto the rocky places, this one is the one hearing the word and straightaway with joy taking it; but he does not have root in himself, but is for a season, and pressure or chasing having come about because of the word, straightaway he is tripped up; and according to Mark: these are the ones being sown onto the rocky places, who whenever they hear the word straightaway with joy take it, and they do not have root in themselves but are for a season, then pressure or chasing having come about because of the word straightaway they are tripped up; and according to Luke: and the ones onto the rock, who whenever they hear with joy welcome the word, and these do not have root, who toward a season believe and in a season of testing stand away. And about those bearing fruit finely, teaching, it says: the one sown onto the fine ground, this one is the one hearing the word and understanding, who indeed bears fruit and makes, this one a hundred, that one sixty, that one thirty; or: and those are the ones sown onto the fine ground, who hear the word and receive it and bear fruit in thirty and in sixty and in a hundred; or: the thing onto the fine ground, these are those who in a fine and good heart having heard the word hold it down and bear fruit in endurance. According to the apostle then, since you are God's farm, God's house-building, farm in the good ground but house-building on the rock, as house-building of God let us stand unshakable toward the winter, and as God's farm let us take no thought for the wicked one, nor for pressure or chasing that comes about because of the word, nor for the anxiety of this age or the cheating of the wealth or the pleasures of the living; but despising all these things let us take up the uncaring spirit of the wisdom, and onto the wealth having in no way cheating let us hurry, and onto the (if I may name them so) pleasures of the garden of luxury let us press, reckoning in each of the toilsome things that the light thing of our pressure for the moment, by excess unto excess, works out for us an age-long weight of glory, while we look out not at the things seen but at the things not seen.
pass_b_english: And since “the sower went out to sow” (Matthew 13:3), let us show that our soul received “his seed” not as “those beside the road”, nor as “the rocky places”, nor as “the thorns”, but as the good earth. That the word of Jesus did not fall “beside the road” or “among the thorns”, as far as it rests with us, we will boast in the Lord (1 Corinthians 1:31). For we have understood what was said; that is why “the evil one” did not snatch away “what was sown in our heart” (Matthew 13:19). And that it was not sown “among the thorns” either, many will bear witness for us, seeing that neither “the care of this age” nor “the deceitfulness of riches” (Matthew 13:22) nor the pleasures of life have been able to hinder the word of God in our souls. It remains for people to be in doubt whether the word of God, as far as it rests with us, came “upon the rocky places” or upon the good earth. For affliction and persecution have come because of the word, and a time of great trial has set in, in which the one “sown upon the rocky places” is shown up, along with those who did not go deep and did not receive Jesus down to the depth of the soul; but the one who “understands the word” “bears fruit” and holds fast to the word to the end “with endurance”, yielding “a hundredfold”.

For we hear how Scripture presents those who, in a time “of affliction or persecution”, stumble after seeming to have received the holy teachings with joy, and who stumble because they have no root but believe for a season. According to Matthew it says, “But the one sown upon the rocky places, this is he who hears the word and at once receives it with joy; yet he has no root in himself but lasts only for a season, and when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, at once he stumbles” (Matthew 13:20-21). According to Mark: “These are the ones sown upon the rocky places, who, when they hear the word, at once receive it with joy, and they have no root in themselves but last only for a season; then, when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, at once they stumble” (Mark 4:16-17). According to Luke: “Those upon the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; and these have no root; they believe for a season, and in a time of trial they fall away” (Luke 8:13). And teaching about those who bear fruit well, it says, “But the one sown upon the good earth, this is he who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, one a hundred, another sixty, another thirty” (Matthew 13:23); or, “And those are the ones sown upon the good earth, who hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold” (Mark 4:20); or, “But that on the good earth, these are the ones who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, hold it fast and bear fruit with endurance” (Luke 8:15).

So, as the apostle says, since “you are God's field, God's building” (1 Corinthians 3:9), a “field” in the good earth and a “building” on the rock, let us stand unshaken against the storm as “God's building”; and as “God's field” let us pay no heed to the evil one, nor to the “affliction or persecution” that comes “because of the word”, nor to the care of this age or the deceitfulness of riches or “the pleasures of life” (Luke 8:14). Rather, despising all these, let us take up the spirit of wisdom that is free from care, and hasten to the riches that hold no deceit at all, and press on to the pleasures, if I may call them that, “of the paradise of delight”. In each of our hardships let us reckon that “the momentary lightness of our affliction is working for us, beyond all measure, an eternal weight of glory, as we look not at the things that are seen but at the things that are not seen” (2 Corinthians 4:17-18).
